subtopics.title: Governance, Statistics and Panchayats
subtopics.summary: This subtopic covers the Panchayat Advancement Index 2.0, which grades rural local bodies on a composite score, and the 2025 National Panchayat Awards. It also covers the ASUSE survey of unincorporated enterprises, and the Public Accounts Committee that reviews government expenditure.
facts: PAI 2.0 was released by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj for FY 2023-24 and covers Gram Panchayats and Traditional Local Bodies.
Panchayat grades are based on a composite score from 0 to 100.
Front Runner (A) covers scores of 75-89 and Performer (B) covers scores of 60-74.
Aspirant (C) covers scores of 40-59 and Beginner (D) covers scores below 40.
PAI 2.0 translates 17 SDGs into 9 Localised Sustainable Development Goals.
Tripura had the highest share of Front Runners among top performers, followed by Kerala and Odisha.
No Panchayat reached the Achiever category in PAI 2.0.
ASUSE 2025 covered the reference period Jan-Dec 2025, as MoSPI replaced the earlier Oct-Sep cycle with a calendar year.
National Panchayat Awards 2025 went to 42 Panchayats from 17 States and UTs, with Karnataka winning the most (6).
The Public Accounts Committee has 22 members (15 Lok Sabha, 7 Rajya Sabha) and was first constituted in 1921.

subtopics.title: Environment and Space Missions
subtopics.summary: MARS is a satellite-based system that detects major methane leaks, and it is being widened to coal mines and waste facilities. SMILE is a joint mission that images how the solar wind interacts with Earth's magnetosphere and ionosphere, helping explain how Earth is shielded from harmful solar radiation.
facts: MARS (Methane Alert and Response System) is a satellite-based system designed to detect and help mitigate major methane leaks.
MARS was launched at COP27 (Sharm el-Sheikh) in 2022 and was developed under UNEP's International Methane Emissions Observatory.
MARS is expanding to coal mines and waste facilities; earlier it focused only on the oil and gas sector.
Methane has much greater short-term warming potential than carbon dioxide.
China, the United States and India rank among the world's largest methane emitters.
The Global Methane Pledge aims to cut global methane emissions by 30% by 2030 compared with 2020 levels; India is not a formal member.
SMILE was launched by ESA and the Chinese Academy of Sciences aboard a Vega-C rocket from French Guiana.
SMILE stands for Solar Wind Magnetosphere Ionosphere Link Explorer.
SMILE provides simultaneous X-ray and ultraviolet imaging of Earth's magnetosphere.
SMILE helps explain how Earth is protected from harmful solar radiation.

subtopics.title: Regional Groupings: SCO and IORA
subtopics.summary: The SCO is a Eurasian grouping that works to counter terrorism, separatism and extremism, and it gives India access to Central Asia's energy and trade. IORA is a cooperation body for countries bordering the Indian Ocean, and India chairs it for 2025-2027.
facts: SCO emerged from the Shanghai Five (1996) and became the SCO in 2001 after Uzbekistan joined.
The SCO's core objective is regional cooperation to counter terrorism, separatism and extremism.
SCO accounts for about 30% of global GDP and about 40% of the world population.
SCO has 10 members, including India (joined 2017) and four Central Asian nations.
The Council of Heads of States is the SCO's supreme decision-making body, and RATS is based in Tashkent.
The SCO secretariat is in Beijing, and its official languages are Russian and Chinese.
IORA was established in 1997; its vision originated during Nelson Mandela's 1995 visit to India.
IORA has 23 Member States and 12 Dialogue Partners, with its secretariat in Ebene (Mauritius).
IORA cooperation areas include maritime safety and security, fisheries management and disaster risk management.
The Indian Ocean Dialogue was launched in 2013 in Perth; India hosted editions in 2014, 2019 and 2021.

subtopics.title: Anniversaries and Historical Episodes
subtopics.summary: Three historical episodes are tied to recent anniversaries: the Korean War of 1950-53, the Komagata Maru voyage of 1914, and Sikkim's integration with India in 1975. Each shows how wars, migration restrictions or treaties shaped the status of a region or its people.
facts: Japanese occupation of Korea lasted from 1910 to 1945; North and South Korea were established in 1948.
North Korean troops crossed the 38th Parallel on 25 June 1950, and the UN Security Council condemned the invasion.
The Korean Armistice Agreement was signed on 27 July 1953, leading to a ceasefire without a peace treaty.
India chaired the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission and deployed the Custodian Force India for prisoners unwilling to return.
The Komagata Maru (Guru Nanak Jahaz), chartered by Gurdit Singh, carried 376 Indian passengers to Canada in 1914.
Canada's Continuous Journey Regulation (1908) required direct travel from the country of origin; only 24 passengers were allowed to disembark.
After the ship returned to India, British authorities tried to deport passengers at Budge Budge, and troops opened fire.
Under the Indo-Sikkim Treaty (1950), Sikkim became an Indian protectorate, with India controlling defence, external affairs and communications.
The 35th Amendment (1974) gave Sikkim Associate State status, a first in India; a 1975 referendum saw over 97% support for integration.
The 36th Amendment made Sikkim the 22nd state of India on 16 May 1975, and Article 371F protects its identity and land rights.

subtopics.title: Appointments, Peacekeeping and Awards
subtopics.summary: NS Raja Subramani takes over as the third Chief of Defence Staff from 31 May 2026. The subtopic also covers India's record in UN peacekeeping and recent recognitions, including the International Booker Prize 2026 and the Pulitzer Prize.
facts: NS Raja Subramani was appointed the 3rd CDS, succeeding Anil Chauhan from 31 May 2026.
The CDS post was created in 2019 following the Kargil Review Committee (1999) and Shekatkar Committee (2016) recommendations.
A CDS must be below 62 years at appointment, has no fixed tenure, and can hold office up to age 65.
The CDS is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister.
The CDS is Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee and Secretary of the Department of Military Affairs.
Major Abhilasha Barak received the UN Military Gender Advocate Award 2025 for work in UNIFIL, Lebanon.
UN Peacekeeping was founded in 1948; peacekeepers are called Blue Berets or Blue Helmets.
In 2007 India became the first country to deploy an all-women contingent to a UN peacekeeping mission.
Taiwan Travelogue won the International Booker Prize 2026, the first Mandarin Chinese-translated novel to win it.
The Pulitzer Prize is administered by Columbia University and has 23 categories.

quizzes.passage:
The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation is a Eurasian grouping that brings together a number of states from the region. Its core objective is regional cooperation to counter terrorism, separatism and extremism. Its membership grew over time, and India joined in 2017, which strengthened India's engagement with Central Asia, a region where geographical constraints limit direct access. Taken together, the grouping's members account for a large share of the world's economic output and population.

Within the grouping, a regional body coordinates counter-terrorism work and intelligence sharing among members. Its emphasis on security is sometimes seen as overshadowing its economic and development cooperation. Border disputes and political frictions between some members are among the factors that affect constructive engagement.

The Indian Ocean Rim Association is a different kind of body. It is an intergovernmental organisation that promotes cooperation among countries bordering the Indian Ocean. Its areas of cooperation include maritime safety, fisheries management, trade facilitation and disaster risk management. Its vision was shaped during a visit to India by a prominent leader. The association also supports a track-based forum, the Indian Ocean Dialogue, which brings together policymakers, strategic experts and maritime stakeholders. The forum was first launched in Australia, and India has hosted several of its editions.

quizzes.passage:
This passage covers two regional bodies with interests in Asia and the Indian Ocean. The first is a Eurasian grouping that began as a group of five states. It later expanded, and its membership now includes India and several Central Asian states. Its supreme decision-making body is a Council of Heads of States. The grouping accounts for about 30% of global GDP and about 40% of the world population. Its stated aim is regional cooperation against terrorism, separatism and extremism. Its structures include a regional anti-terrorist body that shares intelligence among members. For India, membership offers a route into a region that geography makes hard to reach directly.

The second is an intergovernmental organisation for countries that border the Indian Ocean. It was established in 1997 and has its secretariat in Mauritius. Its vision came out of a 1995 visit to India by a prominent leader. Its areas of cooperation include maritime safety and security, fisheries management and disaster risk management. A track-based forum, the Indian Ocean Dialogue, brings together policymakers, strategists and maritime stakeholders, and its objectives include maritime security cooperation and regional connectivity. The forum is a Track 1.5 diplomatic platform under the association. It was first launched in Australia in 2013, and India has since hosted several editions.

quizzes.passage:
The Korean peninsula was divided after the Second World War, and the division has shaped its politics ever since. A dividing line still marks the border between the two states, and a demilitarised zone lies along it. North Korea came under Soviet influence and South Korea under American influence, which deepened the divide. A war then broke out when troops from the north crossed that line, prompting the UN Security Council to condemn the invasion.

The history of Sikkim also shows how political arrangements can change a region's status. Earlier, British-era treaties had already tied the territory to British India. A Himalayan kingdom ruled by a hereditary royal dynasty came under Indian protection through an agreement, with India taking charge of defence, external affairs and communications. Later, the territory's status changed further, and after a popular vote it became a full state of India. Its identity and land rights are protected by a constitutional provision.

Another episode involves a ship that carried passengers from India towards Canada. The passengers were mostly Sikhs, with some Muslims and Hindus, and they hoped for economic opportunities within the British Empire. Canadian rules required travel directly from the country of origin, and only a small number of passengers were allowed ashore. Local community groups raised funds to challenge the discriminatory laws in court. The ship was eventually sent back to India, where passengers faced a confrontation with British authorities.

quizzes.passage:
Three episodes from the region's history are tied to recent anniversaries. The first concerns the Korean peninsula, which was split into two states after the Second World War. The dividing line has remained a border, and a demilitarised zone runs along it. Soon after the division, troops from one side crossed that line in an invasion that prompted a Security Council condemnation. The fighting ended with an armistice rather than a peace treaty, so the two sides have technically remained at war.

The second episode concerns a Himalayan kingdom whose hereditary monarchs ruled for several centuries. Before its integration, a treaty made it a protectorate, and India controlled its defence, external affairs and communications. Its identity and land rights are protected by a constitutional provision. The territory later became a state of India after a popular vote.

The third episode is a voyage. A ship carried passengers from India towards Canada, where rules required travel directly from the country of origin. Only a few passengers were allowed to disembark, and the ship was eventually sent back. When passengers reached a port near Calcutta, British authorities tried to deport them, and troops opened fire. These events show how wars, migration rules and treaties shaped the status of regions and people.

quizzes.passage:
India's Chief of Defence Staff is a four-star officer who is equivalent in rank to the three service chiefs but functions as a first among equals. The post links the armed forces with civilian political leadership, and the officer advises the defence minister on tri-service military matters. The CDS also serves as Secretary of the Department of Military Affairs in the Ministry of Defence.

The United Nations uses peacekeeping missions, which combine military, police and civilian personnel, to help countries move from conflict to peace. India is among the largest troop contributors to these missions. One such mission supervises the ceasefire between India and Pakistan in Jammu and Kashmir. Action for Peacekeeping, a UN initiative, treats women's full participation as central to peacekeeping performance. In 2025, an Indian officer serving in Lebanon received a UN award for advancing gender equality in peacekeeping.

Recognition in literature and journalism also stands out in this record. A novel translated from Mandarin Chinese recently won a major international prize for translated fiction, the first Mandarin novel to do so. Earlier Booker Prize winners include several novelists from India. The Pulitzer Prize is considered the highest national honour in the United States for journalism, literature and musical composition.

quizzes.passage:
The Chief of Defence Staff is a four-star officer who is equivalent in rank to the three service chiefs but functions as a first among equals. The post links the armed forces with civilian political leadership. The officeholder is Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee and is appointed by a cabinet committee chaired by the Prime Minister. The post has no fixed tenure, and the officer may hold office until the age of 65.

The United Nations runs peacekeeping missions that combine military, police and civilian personnel to help countries move from conflict to peace. Peacekeepers are widely known by a distinctive nickname based on their headgear. India is among the largest troop contributors to these missions. In 2025 an Indian officer serving in a peacekeeping mission in Lebanon received a UN gender advocate award. The award recognises work on gender equality in peacekeeping.

Recognition in literature and journalism is also part of the picture. A Mandarin Chinese novel won a major international prize for translated fiction in 2026. The prize is awarded for a work of fiction originally written in a language other than English. Two journalists won a Pulitzer in an illustrated reporting and commentary category for a report on digital arrest scams.
